subject: Design review: private deployment telemetry export & SIEM integration
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@finserve.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: infosec-team@finserve.com
Date: 2026-05-20 09:12 PDT
Subject: Telemetry + SIEM for Private deployment (FinServe VPC)

Hi Soojin,

We're finalizing our architecture for Redwood Private in our VPC and need a quick run-down of options for exporting logs/metrics/traces into our security stack. A few specific asks:

- Can Redwood push logs/traces directly into Splunk (HEC) in our account, or do we need to stage to S3 first?
- What telemetry formats do you support (OTLP/JSON/CEF/CEF over TCP/syslog)?
- Are there recommended network patterns for agentless vs agent-based delivery (VPC endpoints, PrivateLink, NAT, peering)?
- Any PII redaction or log-sampling recommended for compliance (we need SOC2 + PCI scoping)?

We'd like a short design doc and a list of firewall/egress entries we can give to our network team before a design review. Can you loop in an engineer to cover config details?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Rao
Director of Platform Engineering | FinServe
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@finserve.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20 10:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Telemetry + SIEM for Private deployment (FinServe VPC)

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I put together three architecture patterns (attached PDF) and a short checklist for your network/security teams. TL;DR: we support OTLP and JSON natively, can emit CEF mappings for SIEMs, and you can choose between:

1) Direct HEC via PrivateLink/NAT: Redwood's OTLP Agent (hosted in your VPC) forwards to your Splunk HEC endpoint over TLS. Minimal storage, near-real-time. Requires an egress path to your HEC or a PrivateLink endpoint.

2) Staging to customer S3: Redwood writes compressed daily/hourly objects to a customer-managed S3 bucket (KMS-encrypted). Customer-side ingestion jobs (Lambda/Kinesis) move to Splunk. Good for auditability and bulk ingest but adds latency.

3) OTEL collector in-cluster: Deploy a managed OpenTelemetry Collector we provide inside your subnet; it can forward to multiple backends (Splunk, Kafka, internal SIEM). This gives flexible processing (PII redaction, sampling) before egress.

Network checklist included in the attachment: VPC endpoint for S3 (if using S3), required egress ports (443 for HEC, 514/UDP for syslog if chosen), recommended CIDR allowlists, and cert pinning guidance.

Next steps: I'd like to schedule a 45-min design review with your network and infosec teams. Dev can bring an OTEL config and we can propose a PoC window. Attached: private_telemetry_options.pdf

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20 13:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Telemetry + SIEM for Private deployment (FinServe VPC)

Adding engineering details from the implementation side — quoted below is a concise list we use for PoC setups plus a starter OpenTelemetry collector snippet (attached).

Network / ports
- TLS (443) outbound to Splunk HEC if using HEC over HTTPS. We recommend PrivateLink/VPC endpoint for HEC to avoid public egress.
- S3 Put (443) to customer S3 endpoint if using staging. Ensure VPC endpoint for S3 to keep traffic inside AWS backbone.
- Optional: syslog (UDP 514) if you prefer syslog shipping — note reliability differences.

Security & compliance controls
- Server-side KMS with envelope encryption for S3 objects. We can sign object manifests for auditability.
- PII redaction at the OTEL collector: we support regex-based attribute scrubbing and field hashing before export.
- Sampling: recommended head-based 1% for trace volume when traffic is steady; implement backlog-based adaptive sampling for bursts.

Tracing hooks / headers
- We emit W3C Traceparent and baggage headers. To link app traces to Redwood service traces, include the header x-redwood-request-id in requests.

Collector snippet (OTLP -> Splunk HEC, high-level):
# (attachment: otlp-collector-config.yaml)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
      grpc:
exporters:
  splunk_hec:
    token: "<REDACTED>"
    endpoint: "https://hec.internal.finserve.com:443/services/collector"
processors:
  batch:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: "user.email"
        action: delete
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [splunk_hec]

Operational notes
- We do not export raw model KV cache contents. Model-level debugging logs are sampled and redacted by default.
- For PoC: we can stand up a temporary staging cluster in your VPC for 2 weeks. Our engineering team will need a list of CIDRs and a service account with minimal permissions.

— Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that is very helpful. A few quick answers and asks from our side:

- Infosec prefers PrivateLink to avoid public egress. We'll open a request for a Splunk HEC endpoint via our connectivity team.
- For PCI scoping, we want PII redaction at the collector and a 90-day hot retention with 365-day cold archive. Can you confirm Redwood will honor object lifecycle and encryption requirements when writing to our S3?
- Please include a short confluence page with the exact IAM policy for the PoC service account and the minimal ports/CIDRs for our firewall team.

Let's book the design review for next Wednesday 11am PT if that works. Also looping in infosec (infosec-team@finserve.com) for approvals.
